title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## LBA-CBF Safety Filter

### The Breakthrough
The authors present Look‑Back Adaptive Control Barrier Functions (LBA‑CBF), a safety filter that evaluates up to 250,000 dynamics models in parallel using a short look‑back window and enforces CBF constraints on all models near the best fit. By ranking candidate models and applying a high‑order CBF condition, the method guarantees safety without explicit model switching. Experiments on a Crazyflie quadrotor and an F1TENTH car show the system adapting to sudden wind, payload changes, and varying tire‑road friction while reaching goals safely.

### The Caveats
The paper compares only to vague “adaptive and robust baselines” without naming or benchmarking against standard state‑of‑the‑art methods, leaving the breadth of improvement unclear.

## PEARS Tactile Adaptation

### The Breakthrough
PEARS introduces a hybrid RL framework that adapts pretrained tactile manipulation policies online by combining physics‑guided force reasoning (via a vision‑language model) with diffusion‑steered policy perturbations. The force reasoning module infers contact‑force bounds from visual and tactile histories, while diffusion steering adjusts the latent noise of a frozen flow‑matching policy to correct motion errors without retraining the base network. Real‑world experiments on two tactile tasks report large success‑rate gains over the original policies.

### The Caveats
The work does not benchmark PEARS against any existing tactile‑manipulation baselines, so the significance of the reported gains is uncertain.

## JengaBot LLM Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
A hobbyist uses Claude to generate control code that autonomously trains a tabletop robot arm to locate, grasp, and place Jenga blocks after an overnight run. The system incorporates a cardboard Pez‑style dispenser for repeatable block feeding and a webcam‑based virtual leader that mirrors a human arm to bootstrap data for a vision‑language‑action model. This demonstrates that large language models can orchestrate both software and simple hardware adaptations without continual human tele‑operation.

### The Caveats
The demo is anecdotal, with no quantitative metrics or baseline comparison, so the autonomous pick‑and‑place capability remains unverified.

## 10‑DOF 3D‑Printed Biped

### The Breakthrough
A 10‑degree‑of‑freedom bipedal robot built from 3D‑printed parts uses only eight LX‑116A servos, leveraging two passive joints to achieve full locomotion, including walking, sitting, standing, kicking, and turning. The project releases all CAD files, an Arduino servo library, and a detailed build guide, enabling rapid replication and modification for low‑cost robotics enthusiasts.

### The Caveats
The platform is demonstrated only via a YouTube video and lacks quantitative performance data or comparisons to existing bipedal robots, leaving its claimed capabilities unverified.

## QF3 Fast Flow RL

### The Breakthrough
QF3 augments flow‑matching RL with filtered Q‑gradients that back‑propagate only through action dimensions staying close to replayed actions, enabling a ten‑fold wall‑clock speedup over the prior FPO++ method. The approach trains humanoid locomotion policies from scratch and fine‑tunes flow‑based manipulation policies, claiming zero‑shot transfer to real hardware.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no quantitative performance numbers or ablation studies to substantiate the reported speedup and zero‑shot transfer claims.

## DepthWorld World Model

### The Breakthrough
DepthWorld combines a calibration pipeline that fuses learned stereo depth with a factor‑graph to achieve <0.7 px reprojection error on 90 % of episodes, and a video‑diffusion model that jointly predicts multi‑view RGB and dense metric depth for manipulation. Depth supervision improves RGB prediction quality by +1.48 dB PSNR over an RGB‑only baseline and yields accurate metric depth for geometric reasoning.

### The Caveats
The benefits for manipulation are unsubstantiated, as the work evaluates only static dataset metrics without downstream planning or real‑robot experiments.

## HUMXN Home Service Data

### The Breakthrough
HUMXN subsidizes plumbing, electrical, and HVAC service calls in three U.S. cities, pairing each appointment with technician‑worn capture hardware that records first‑person video, tool usage, diagnostics, and decision steps, aiming to build a large, structured dataset of skilled‑trade demonstrations.

### The Caveats
The program is announced without independent validation or concrete metrics showing that the collected data improves robot learning.

## CROWD Pedestrian Dataset

### The Breakthrough
The CROWD repository automates extraction of 34,000 hours of YouTube dashcam footage from 238 countries, runs YOLOv11 detection, and assembles the largest cross‑cultural pedestrian behavior dataset with 75,903 videos covering 9,942 cities, facilitating statistical analysis of road‑crossing behavior for autonomous‑vehicle planning.

### The Caveats
YOLOv11 detections are never validated across the diverse dash‑cam sources, so annotation quality and downstream AV research reliability remain unproven.

## Spirula Studio 3D Reconstruction

### The Breakthrough
Spirula Studio is a C++ tool that trains 3D Gaussian Splatting models directly from photos or video using a Vulkan‑based compute backend, fitting up to 10 million Gaussians into 8 GB VRAM and eliminating the need for Python, PyTorch, or external COLMAP pipelines. It integrates a lightweight Structure‑from‑Motion module, AI‑based masking, and exposure correction, supporting 360° and fisheye inputs for fast, VRAM‑efficient reconstruction.

### The Caveats
The repository provides only demo videos and no quantitative benchmarks or comparisons to existing reconstruction pipelines, leaving claimed efficiency and quality unverified.

## OpenHarness AI Coding Harness

### The Breakthrough
OpenHarness is an open‑source Dart application that runs multiple AI coding agents (Claude, Codex, Cursor, etc.) side‑by‑side across laptops, servers, and devices via peer‑to‑peer WebRTC with ChaCha20‑Poly1305 and X25519 encryption, avoiding SSH and port‑forwarding. It achieves 11‑13 ms UI latency and ~0.1 % CPU usage while handling 16 terminals and 1,000 scrollback lines per pane.

### The Caveats
Latency and CPU‑usage numbers are unsubstantiated, lacking baseline comparisons to existing agent‑orchestration platforms.

### Priority
LBA‑CBF stands out as the most actionable development today because it delivers a provably safe, real‑world‑tested safety filter that can instantly improve the reliability of quadrotor and ground‑vehicle deployments.

### One action
Review the LBA‑CBF implementation details and consider integrating its parallel model‑ranking safety layer into any existing quadrotor or mobile‑robot control stack.

### What to watch
The manipulation‑focused stories (JengaBot, PEARS, and QF3) illustrate a trend toward leveraging large language models, physics‑guided reasoning, and flow‑based RL to reduce manual engineering and accelerate policy adaptation. While JengaBot showcases low‑cost LLM‑driven data collection, PEARS adds tactile feedback and diffusion steering for online adaptation, and QF3 pushes training efficiency. Future work will likely blend these approaches, combining LLM‑generated data pipelines with physics‑aware adaptation and fast RL training.
